A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and can be matched across moves and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original accuracy, token-use, retrieval, and failure-mode results for eleven model configurations on ChemKGMultiHopQA.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds Gold+CoT evaluations and analyses relating oracle-context length to accuracy and iterative recoveries.

M1.justification: The iterative controller retains its five-step budget, partial-answer state, top-10 retrieval, and compact passage history. Gold+CoT is introduced as a comparison baseline, without changing the evaluated iterative method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same chemistry benchmark with one- to four-hop questions. Table S5 discusses nine alternative datasets but does not report running the systems on them. The new context-length analyses reuse existing coverage.

E2.justification: Section 4.1 and Table 2 introduce Gold+CoT for GPT-4o and Claude 3.7 Sonnet Standard and Thinking. This materially strengthens the central comparison by testing static oracle evidence with explicit reasoning. Thinking matches the previously evaluated Reasoning configuration; the original comparators remain.

E3.justification: v3 adds the static Gold+CoT prompting protocol and context-length binning. Figure 11(a) changes its stated population from all questions to No-Context-wrong questions, correcting its inconsistency with the diagnostic scope; Figure 13(a) also explicitly identifies this filtering. These changes do not establish reruns of the retained benchmark experiments.

E4.justification: The new Gold+CoT ablation directly tests whether additional reasoning explains the iterative advantage. Appendix S1.7 and Figures S13–S14 separately examine context overload through length-stratified accuracy and recovery distributions. These add substantial checks of competing explanations for the paper's central finding.

E5.justification: Uncertainty documentation changes locally: Figure 13 retains error bars but removes v1's description of them as across-model variance, while Figure S13 explicitly specifies one-standard-deviation bars. Existing t-tests remain, and no repeated-run counts or seed information are added.

E6.justification: Table 1 is unchanged, but Table 2 substantially changes the evidence about the iterative advantage: GPT-4o reaches 78.08% with Gold+CoT, compared with 56.32% under original Gold Context and 81.96% under Iterative RAG. Revised diagnostic populations yield replacement results, including overconfident accuracy of 61.5% versus 71.4%, and no-latch/latch accuracy of 84.8%/30.9% versus 89.5%/37.1%. New context-length findings are also reported.

T1.justification: The diagnostic definitions and equations for suppression, coverage impact, token scaling, variability, and procedural compliance are retained. No new theorem, proof, formal assumption, or substantive mathematical derivation appears.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions and claims, including eleven-model evaluation, iterative superiority over Gold Context, gains up to approximately 25.6 percentage points, and mechanism-level diagnostics.

C2.justification: v3 acknowledges that explicit static reasoning closes much of the performance gap and argues that output length and oracle-context length do not fully explain the remaining advantage. Appendix S1.6 explicitly identifies single-benchmark generalization as a limitation, while S1.7 cautions that the length trend is inconclusive and the longest bins are sparse.

D1.justification: Figure S12 supplies the exact Gold+CoT prompt, and Section 3.1 expands documentation of oracle evidence and passage lengths. The abstract's code/results hyperlink changes from a named GitHub repository to an anonymous.4open.science repository; the PDFs establish the destination change, not its availability.

R1.justification: Table S5 and Appendix S1.6 expand dataset positioning through candidates including DocHopQA, BioHopR, and Koblex, with corresponding references. A few model-source references disappear. The main related-work taxonomy and novelty positioning remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 consolidates the repetitive methodology introduction, rewrites selected Gold Context and dataset explanations, and adds focused subsections for Gold+CoT, dataset selection, and context length. Most existing prose and the overall narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds Tables 2 and S5, the prompt display in Figure S12, and plots S13–S14. Figures 11(a) and 13(a) are redrawn with filtering labels, and several displays move through reflow. The original compliance table becomes Table 3; most existing visual content and formatting are retained.

improvement.justification: The stronger static reasoning baseline addresses an important missing control, while corrected diagnostic filtering and explicit generalization limits improve interpretability. Gold+CoT reveals that much of the original advantage can be recovered without iterative retrieval. The improvement remains limited: the control covers only three configurations, does not match total computation, and leaves the broad mechanistic claims largely unchanged.
